counterfactual_missing_items: but the bleeding source could not be identified
no history of trauma or prior renal procedures
expanding hematoma within and outside the renal capsule
decisive_items: a large retroperitoneal hemorrhage surrounding the right kidney extending into the pelvis
heterogeneous echogenicity around the right renal parenchyma
A repeat CT scan showed an expanding hematoma within and outside the renal capsule, suggesting a renal or renovascular source of bleeding
response.rationale: R2 best integrates the acute flank pain, perirenal echogenicity, retroperitoneal hemorrhage, and expanding renal/renovascular hematoma as spontaneous renal hemorrhage. R3 is the directly imaged finding but lacks the renal-source completeness central to the diagnosis. R4 and R1 propose specific vascular lesions that were never identified and are disfavored by absence of trauma, prior procedures, or an angiographic source. R6 invokes infarction without CT or clinical evidence of renal infarction.

rejected.why: No imaging or clinical evidence of renal infarction; the findings are hemorrhagic rather than ischemic.
No trauma or prior renal procedures and no pseudoaneurysm or AVF demonstrated; bleeding source was not identified.
Renal artery aneurysm rupture is speculative; no aneurysm or vascular lesion was identified on CT.
